truth.claim: ceiling 1.43x = 100/70; half the hours -> never more than 2x
IBM Credit: 7 days, 5 desks, 90 minutes of work, 4 hours after
truth.note: Hammer & Champy 1993 ch. 3 and Davenport & Nohria 1994 as cited; the honest limits say it is the authors' account, not an audit; strip geometry 15.75 and 42 of 588 units recompute

defects.what: The pin labelled TRUE reads '1.43x / HOUR 70' once the ceiling is drawn; the answer to the committed question is 1.37x (hour 73) and the ceiling is a different quantity (instant drafting). Labelled 'THE CEILING' above, but the TRUE pin changes value under the viewer
'UNTOUCHED 45' is a mid-tick counter while the caption already says '70 hours untouched'
The honest line ('A teaching model, not IBM's numbers. Faster work can also move the queues.') is on the stage only; the captions and transcript carry only the Monday question
'90 MINUTES OF WORK' is set in a pale tint above the strip while the strip itself is a hatched block; the sliver that is the point is hard to find at a glance

one_line: One row of 100 hours that closes up to 73 is exactly the right count, and the pins put promise, guess and truth on one axis; just do not let the TRUE pin move to the ceiling.
